Project 
 The Woodfibre LNG Project is located approximately 7 km west-southwest of Squamish, British Columbia. It involves the construction and operation of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) export facility on the previous Woodfibre pulp mill site, which would have a storage capacity of 250,000 m3 and would produce approximately 2.1 million tons per year of LNG.
 Woodfibre Management Ltd. is a privately held Canadian company based in Vancouver and a subsidiary of Pacific Energy Corporation Limited.
 Job Summary 
 Woodfibre LNG is seeking an experienced Analyzer Technician to join our dynamic team. Reporting to the Electrical & Instrumentation Supervisor , the successful candidate will support preventive, predictive, corrective, turnaround, and emergency maintenance activities. Key responsibilities include installing, calibrating, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing process analyzers, analyzer sample conditioning systems, and associated instrumentation to ensure accurate and reliable process measurements. The successful candidate will also provide support for general instrumentation maintenance & Turnaround activities as required. This role offers an opportunity to be part of a dedicated team, ensuring the safe, reliable, efficient, and environmentally responsible operation of the Woodfibre LNG facility.
 Key Responsibilities : 
 The successful applicant will:
 Support start-up and operations of the LNG plant 
 Troubleshoot and repair process analyzers such as Gas Chromatographs, Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems (CEMS), Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) analyzers, moisture analyzers, oxygen analyzers, and associated analyzer sample conditioning systems.
 Troubleshoot and repair ABB PGC5000 and PGC1000 Gas Chromatographs, ABB AO2000 Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS), ABB RVP4501 Analyzer, and associated analyzer equipment.
 Assist with the maintenance, troubleshooting, calibration, and repair of other process instrumentation and control systems, as required, to support plant operations and maintenance activities.
 Utilize remote connectivity and digital support platforms, as required, to perform diagnostics, configuration, testing, troubleshooting, and maintenance of analyzer systems in collaboration with Operations, Engineering, OEMs, and third-party service providers
 Support Process Safety Management - Maintain analyzer systems that support process safety, environmental compliance, and operational integrity. SIS awareness, Alarm philosophy, Functional Safety
 Inspect, test, calibrate, and validate analyzer systems to ensure accurate and reliable process measurements using electrical, electronic, pneumatic, and analytical testing equipment.
 Perform scheduled preventive, predictive, and emergency maintenance on analyzer systems, completing all maintenance reports, calibration records, and equipment history documentation.
 Perform mechanical work associated with analyzer repair and modification, including the removal and installation of tubing, sample lines, regulators, filters, sample conditioning equipment, and analyzer components.
 Perform analyzer calibration using certified calibration gases and reference standards while maintaining measurement accuracy and compliance with manufacturer recommendations.
 Troubleshoot analyzer communication interfaces with the ICSS, PLCs, and associated control systems.
 Provide day-to-day support to ensure maximum reliability and availability of analyzer systems while working towards achieving plant reliability goals and measuring the effectiveness of maintenance programs.
 Review process flow diagrams, analyzer drawings, sample system drawings, equipment lists, and technical specifications to develop and execute maintenance activities.
 Collaborate with Operations, Engineering, Reliability, and third-party analyzer service providers to support plant performance and reliability.
 Contribute to the continuous improvement of maintenance key performance indicators.
 HSSE 
 100% compliance with company HSE policies and guidelines.
 Champion HSE as a member of the LNG Operations Team.
 Lead HSE Shift Meeting/ safety walks/audits if and when required.
 Timely intervention to mitigate risks and ensure the safety of personnel and plant.
 Demonstrate a personal commitment to influence overall safety behavior in the plant.
 Safeguarding systems check lists are implemented/completed by Shift Operations to agreed frequencies and standards.
 Execute plant wide operations hazards awareness program. 
 Initiate inputs for plant risk register and mitigation tracking process for operations.
 Required Experience 
 Minimum of 5+ years of relevant industrial maintenance experience.
 A valid BC Journeyman Instrumentation Technician Certificate or Red Seal Instrumentation Technician certification. Dual ticket would be an asset. 
 Experience with ABB PGC5000, ABB PGC1000, ABB AO2000 CEMS, and ABB RVP4501 analyzers.
 Experience with analyzer sample conditioning systems and calibration gas systems.
 Knowledge of regulatory requirements in BC
 Proficiency with Yokogawa control systems.
 Commissioning and start-up experience.
 Knowledge of DCS systems, PLCs, HMI systems, and industrial communications.
 Experience with analyzer calibration, validation, and troubleshooting.
 Previous experience using a Project Resource Manager (PRM) and Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS), such as SAP.
 Additional Requirements 
 Energetic in pursuit of continuous improvement processes.
 Experience working with large multi-disciplinary teams, and contractors in a multicultural environment is an asset. 
 Communication/interpersonal skills – to be able to interact with front line workers through to management and all hierarchical levels. 
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
 Motivated and willing to take ownership of tasks.
 Ability to work well under pressure and handle multiple tasks, targets and changing priorities within tight time frames.
 Shares knowledge readily and encourages personal development.
 Demonstrated computer knowledge with experience in Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel, etc.
 A valid driver’s license (with abstract) and passport.
 Must be legally entitled to work in Canada.
 This role will be a combination of office and site-based role.
 The position is based in Squamish, BC (Project Site), and work in the Company’s Vancouver Office as required . 
 Only qualified candidates legally entitled to work in Canada will be contacted.

 We are looking for a Principal Engineer to help build GitLab Duo Agent Platform, the agentic orchestration layer that runs AI agents and flows across the entire software lifecycle.
 Principal Engineers at GitLab are recognized experts across multiple technology domains and represent the senior technical leadership within their organization. In this role you will set technical direction for a significant part of the Agent Platform, working across several teams to turn agentic capabilities into something engineering organizations can actually depend on: predictable, observable, governable, and fast enough to sit in the critical path of real development work.
 The Agent Platform is not a single service. It spans agent execution and orchestration, flow definition and event-driven triggering, the AI Catalog through which customers discover and manage agents, model routing and evaluation, and the governance surface that decides which agents may act where and under whose identity. It runs on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and Self-Managed installations, including deployments that use self-hosted models to meet compliance requirements. You will work on the parts of that system where the hard architectural questions live, and you will do it hands-on.
 This role reports into the VP of the AI Engineering organization and works closely with Engineering Managers, Staff Engineers, Product Management, Infrastructure and Security.
 What you'll do 
 Define the technical direction for a significant area of Duo Agent Platform across several teams, and partner with Engineering Managers and Product to turn it into a roadmap with a six-month horizon.
 Build the orchestration layer that makes agents and flows reliable: session lifecycle, tool invocation, context assembly, concurrency, retries, timeouts, and failure modes that degrade gracefully instead of stalling a developer's workflow.
 Hands on work on driving topics throughout the whole organisation from POC level, architecture to full implementation. 
 Participate in Incident Management on-call rotation, to help meet availability goals for GitLab.com.
 Strong product builder and ownership mentality. Understanding of product strategy, technical strategy, delivering customer value and iteration towards a successful product
 Write clear, opinionated design documents, architecture narratives, and decision records that let other teams make aligned decisions. Ensure the architecture holds across multi-tenant GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments, including self-hosted model configurations, and respects data governance boundaries in each.
 Use the platform on our own work, find where it falls short of what we claim, and feed that back through improvements into the product.
 Mentor Staff and Senior Engineers, and raise the bar for experimentation rigor and cross-team collaboration.
 Work across the whole platform on different projects, features and teams. This reaches across:
 Design the extensibility surface so customers can build custom agents and flows, connect their own tools and internal systems, and bring external agents such as Claude Code and Codex into GitLab workflows without weakening the platform's guarantees.
 Drive down the cost and latency of agentic requests, and work with Product on how model selection, routing, and credit consumption behave as usage grows.
 Define the evaluation practice for the platform: offline benchmarks and online experiments that measure task completion, correctness, tool-call accuracy, latency, and cost per task, and that catch regressions before customers do.
 Build the governance and safety surface with Security and Compliance: policy-driven controls over which agents and models may run where, permission and identity semantics that align to existing roles and group structure, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, traceability of every flow session, and audit that stands up to enterprise review.
 Complete Interview Training and participate in hiring for the department as a technical interviewer or panel member.
 What you'll bring 
 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years at Staff, Principal level or equivalent senior technical leadership.
 Hands-on production experience building on large language models: agent loops, tool calling, context management, retrieval, prompt and model evaluation. Experience shipping this to real users, not only prototyping it.
 Strong background in distributed systems, including service decomposition, fault tolerance, observability, and operational resilience under multi-tenant load.
 A track record of defining evaluation frameworks and using benchmark and experiment results to make architecture decisions, rather than shipping on intuition.
 Experience designing human-in-the-loop controls, safety guardrails, and responsible AI practices for systems that act on a customer's behalf.
 Ability to drive alignment across Engineering, Product, Infrastructure, and Security on problems that start out ambiguous.
 Experience mentoring senior engineers and shaping technical direction across multiple teams without direct authority.
 Comfort working in one or more of Ruby, Go, Python, or TypeScript, and willingness to work across the stack the platform spans.
 Excellent written and asynchronous communication, and the ability to work effectively in a fully remote, globally distributed organization.
 About the team 
 The AI engineering organisation is building the product and infrastructure that make GitLab an effective environment for running agents across the software development lifecycle. We’re distributed across the world and partner with teams throughout GitLab to help the GitLab Duo Agent Platform become the backbone of GitLab's AI features. You will report directly to the VP of Engineering for AI and especially work together with all the teams, the engineering management and other principal engineers in the AI department.  Qui nous sommes: 
Quadbridge est un fournisseur nord-américain de solutions informatiques en pleine croissance, qui permet aux entreprises de relever quotidiennement des défis complexes grâce à des partenariats solides avec des fournisseurs de technologies de pointe et à une étroite collaboration avec notre équipe et nos clients.

Nous sommes Quadbridge.
 Aperçu du rôle 
 L’analyste d’affaires en IA agit à titre de lien entre les parties prenantes de l’entreprise chez Quadbridge et l’équipe de mise en œuvre des solutions du Centre d’excellence en IA. Vous travaillerez directement avec les différentes équipes de l’organisation afin de comprendre leurs défis d’affaires et de les traduire en exigences claires et concrètes en matière d’intelligence artificielle et d’automatisation. Vous demeurerez également impliqué tout au long de la livraison des solutions en collaborant avec les architectes IA, les développeurs d’applications IA et les ingénieurs de données afin de vous assurer que les solutions développées répondent réellement aux besoins d’affaires.
 Principales responsabilités 
 Les tâches et responsabilités comprennent notamment :
 Collaborer avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise et les ambassadeurs IA afin de recueillir, clarifier et documenter les exigences liées à l’intelligence artificielle et à l’automatisation.
 Traduire les besoins d’affaires en exigences fonctionnelles claires, en récits utilisateurs (user stories) et en critères d’acceptation pour les solutions IA.
 Animer des ateliers de découverte, des entrevues avec les parties prenantes et des séances de collecte des besoins afin de cerner les opportunités d’utilisation de l’IA, en s’appuyant sur la cartographie des capacités de Quadbridge.
 Évaluer et classifier les cas d’utilisation potentiels selon la matrice de criticité des cas d’usage de Quadbridge et contribuer au processus de révision technique du Centre d’excellence en IA.
 Participer activement à l’équipe de mise en œuvre des solutions IA tout au long du cycle de livraison, en collaboration avec les architectes IA, les développeurs d’applications IA et les ingénieurs de données.
 Gérer et prioriser le carnet de produits (backlog) des initiatives d’IA et d’automatisation du Centre d’excellence en IA, en équilibrant les besoins des parties prenantes avec la capacité de livraison.
 Définir et suivre les indicateurs de performance clés (KPI) des solutions IA en partenariat avec les responsables d’affaires.
 Soutenir les activités d’acceptation utilisateur (UAT), la documentation des solutions et la gestion du changement afin d’encourager l’adoption.
 Maintenir l’inventaire des cas d’utilisation et des agents IA du Centre d’excellence en IA, incluant leur objectif déclaré, leur propriétaire et leur niveau de criticité.
 Agir comme point de contact principal pour les ambassadeurs IA qui proposent de nouveaux cas d’utilisation provenant de leurs unités d’affaires.
 Qualifications 
 Minimum de 3 ans d’expérience démontrée à titre d’analyste d’affaires, de propriétaire de produit (Product Owner) ou dans un rôle similaire, idéalement dans des initiatives technologiques ou liées à l’IA et à l’automatisation.
 Excellentes compétences en gestion des parties prenantes et capacité à transformer des besoins d’affaires parfois ambigus en exigences claires et structurées.
 Bonne connaissance pratique des concepts et des capacités de l’intelligence artificielle et de l’IA générative.
 Expérience avec les techniques de collecte des exigences, telles que les récits utilisateurs (user stories), la cartographie des processus et l’animation d’ateliers.
 Compréhension du cycle de vie des solutions d’IA et d’automatisation, de l’idéation jusqu’au déploiement.
 Aisance à travailler avec des équipes techniques multidisciplinaires, comprenant des architectes, des développeurs et des ingénieurs de données.
 Excellentes aptitudes en communication orale et écrite, avec la capacité de documenter clairement les exigences pour des publics techniques et non techniques.
 Expérience avec des outils de gestion et de priorisation de backlog (ex. : Azure DevOps, Jira).
 Atouts 
 Connaissance de Microsoft Foundry et/ou de Copilot Studio .
 Expérience avec les cadres de gouvernance de l’IA ou les approches de classification des risques et de la criticité des cas d’utilisation.
 Expérience en amélioration des processus, gestion du changement ou cartographie des capacités d’affaires.
 Expérience dans un environnement de services professionnels ou en soutien à des clients.
 Formation et certifications 
 Diplôme d’études collégiales ou universitaires en administration des affaires, technologies de l’information, informatique ou dans un domaine connexe.

 Operating Model & Segmentation

 About Mila 
 Founded by Professor Yoshua Bengio of the Université de Montréal, Mila brings together researchers specializing in artificial intelligence, and more specifically in machine learning, deep learning and reinforcement learning. HELLO!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. I’m excited to share that we’re hiring our first Support Engineering Manager in AMER.

Support Engineering is the technical bridge between frontline Support, Product, and Engineering. The team investigates complex product and customer issues, helps confirm which problems truly require code changes, and enables the broader Support organization to resolve more issues independently. We’re looking for a hands-on leader to make that bridge stronger as the function grows—aligning technical rigor with Ashby’s broader standards for customer success.

This is not a traditional Support Manager role. You’ll manage and mentor Support Engineers, stay close to complex investigations, and work with Engineering and Product to improve how technical issues are diagnosed, escalated, and resolved. You’ll help define the standards and systems that let a small, highly technical team move quickly without sacrificing judgment or quality.




ABOUT THE ROLE

When a complex issue moves beyond frontline Support, Support Engineering investigates the problem using customer context, application behavior, logs, databases, integrations, APIs, and code-level context. The team determines whether the issue can be resolved through configuration, data correction, documentation, enablement, or an in-app change—or whether it is a product defect that Engineering needs to fix. Your role is to make that path clearer and more effective: develop a deep understanding of how each partner team works, coach the investigation, and ensure escalations meet a shared standard for evidence, ownership, and customer impact.

You’ll lead the team’s day-to-day technical development while building the connective tissue around it. That includes reviewing investigations and escalations, mentoring Support Engineers through ambiguous problems, clarifying triage and handoff practices, identifying recurring patterns, and partnering with frontline Support, Product, and Engineering on durable improvements. You’ll help ensure Support Engineering scales in a way that reflects Ashby’s broader expectations for customer success—not simply by passing issues between teams, but by resolving more issues independently and making the right problems easier for Engineering to act on.

As the first Support Engineering Manager at Ashby, you’ll have meaningful influence over how the function grows. You’ll balance people leadership with hands-on technical judgment, make pragmatic decisions with incomplete information, and focus the team on the work that most improves customer outcomes, strengthens cross-functional trust, and protects Engineering time.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Lead, coach, and develop Support Engineers through regular feedback, technical mentorship, career development, and clear expectations for ownership and judgment.

 - Stay close to complex investigations by reviewing technical work, joining escalations when useful, and coaching the team on APIs, integrations, logs, databases, data issues, configuration, and product behavior.

 - Build shared operating standards across Support, Support Engineering, Product, and Engineering that help frontline Support resolve more issues independently, reduce customer effort, and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable escalations when code changes are needed.

 - Partner with Engineering and Product to synthesize recurring customer patterns, validate defects, improve supportability, and determine whether the right solution is a code change, documentation, tooling, enablement, or process improvement.

 - Identify the highest-leverage friction in the team’s workflows and ship practical improvements to tooling, diagnostics, routing, documentation, and operating processes.

 - Hire and onboard future Support Engineers, help define the team’s career path, and build a scalable model for technical growth as the function expands across regions.

 - Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, frontline self-sufficiency, customer effort, recurring issue reduction, and Engineering time spent on confirmed defects and roadmap work.


YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

 - You have direct people-management experience leading a technical support, developer support, production support, or support engineering team in a B2B SaaS or similarly complex software environment.

 - You are energized by hands-on people leadership: reviewing work, giving precise feedback, raising technical judgment, and helping strong engineers grow.

 - You have coached an Engineer through a specific technical or judgment gap and can point to what changed as a result.

 - You have enough technical depth to reason about APIs, integrations, logs, databases, application behavior, and code-level context—and to coach others through ambiguous investigations.

 - You know how to distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect, and can help a team make that decision with evidence.

 - You have improved an escalation, triage, or support-to-Engineering workflow and can explain what changed, why you changed it, and how you measured the result.

 - You build structure without over-engineering. You can make clear decisions with incomplete information, ship a useful first version, and iterate based on what you learn. You’ve stood up processes, workflows, or standards from scratch.

 - You communicate clearly and thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences, especially when explaining tradeoffs, uncertainty, customer impact, and recommended action.


YOU SHOULD NOT APPLY IF

 - You have not yet directly managed a team, and your leadership experience has primarily been through mentorship, project leadership, or team-lead responsibilities. This role requires direct people-management experience, including accountability for team development, feedback, and day-to-day management.

 - You’re looking primarily for a traditional queue-management or people-management role where you can stay removed from technical investigations and escalation quality.

 - Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, infrastructure, cloud operations, or systems administration without substantial experience debugging customer-impacting SaaS applications and integrations.

 - You prefer to optimize processes from a distance rather than work directly with engineers on the details of diagnosis, evidence, and technical judgment.

 - You see Support Engineering primarily as a pass-through queue to Engineering rather than an investigation and enablement layer that should resolve more issues independently.

 - You’re uncomfortable operating in a growing function where ownership boundaries, workflows, and success measures will continue to evolve.

 - You prefer prolonged analysis or perfect certainty over making a well-reasoned decision, learning quickly, and improving the system in motion.

Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. BENEFITS

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby—do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 The Role

 In this elite, high-impact role, you will act as a technical and strategic powerhouse, operating directly on the front lines with XTM’s largest enterprise customers and prospects. You will own the entire lifecycle of our AI capabilities—from initial value definition and custom Proofs of Concept (PoCs) to advanced workflow deployment and continuous optimization.
 This is not a traditional support or back-office engineering role. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will combine deep technical expertise in AI/LLMs with the consultative skills required to redesign localization workflows for global brands, drastically reducing Time-to-Value (TTV).
 This is an individual contributor role, and the successful candidate will not have direct people-management responsibilities.
 Scope of Tasks
 1. End-to-End AI Value Delivery & PoCs
 Proof of Concept Ownership: Design, build, and technical-validate custom AI-driven localization workflows during the pre-sales and expansion phases to outmaneuver competition.
 Deployment & Integration: Lead the technical onboarding and deployment of XTM’s AI features, ensuring seamless integration via APIs with clients' existing content management systems (CMS) and data pipelines.
 Value Definition: Partner with clients at the onset to map their baseline metrics (e.g., translation memory leverage, MT edit distance, cost-per-word, turnaround times) and align XTM’s AI capabilities with their strategic business goals.
 2. Workflow Consulting & Change Management
 Workflow Engineering: Audit clients' legacy localization setups and architect automated, AI-first workflows within XTM (leveraging advanced AI matching, automated tagging, and LLM capabilities).
 Enterprise Advisory: Act as a trusted advisor, guiding enterprise localization teams through the operational change management required to transition to AI-augmented translation models.
 3. Continuous Optimization & Feedback Loop
 Adoption & Enhancement: Monitor post-onboarding feature utilization, proactively identifying opportunities to tune AI models, refine prompts, and unlock deeper ROI for the customer.
 R&D Linchpin: Act as the direct, unfiltered feedback loop between customer production realities and XTM’s Product/R&D teams, channeling real-world edge cases into core product enhancement.
 Core AI Competencies & "Natural Curiosity"
 Deep AI Literacy: A profound, self-driven interest in the evolution of Artificial Intelligence. You don't just use AI; you understand how Large Language Models (LLMs), prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and neural machine translation (NMT) operate under the hood.

Qui nous sommes
Chez Ecosystem, tout part de ces convictions : se responsabiliser et garantir le résultat final. C’est pourquoi nous prenons en charge l’ingénierie et la construction des projets, de la conception à l’exécution, jusqu’à la mise en service. Rien ne nous arrête pour répondre efficacement aux défis énergétiques et de décarbonation de l’environnement bâti. 
Ecosystem compte parmi ses réalisations récentes d’importants projets d’amélioration énergétique au CIUSSS de la Capitale-Nationale, l’Université de Toronto et au San Diego Padres Stadium. 
Qui vous êtes
Vous êtes un ingénieur curieux, créatif et proactif qui connait bien les systèmes électromécaniques. Vous êtes passionné par les solutions énergétiques intelligentes. En tant que membre d’une équipe multidisciplinaire et innovante composée d’ingénieurs stimulés par les défis techniques. Vous voulez contribuer au succès de projets de plusieurs millions de dollars. 
Ce que vous ferez
Chez Ecosystem, vous ne travaillerez pas sur des projets standards avec des solutions toutes faites. Vous interviendrez sur des bâtiments existants, énergivores et complexes, conçus à une époque où l’énergie coûtait peu. Chaque mandat est unique et demande réflexion, créativité et débrouillardise.
Vous participerez au développement de projets de performance énergétique, de l’audit, en passant par la construction, jusqu’à la validation des résultats.  Développer des mesures d’efficacité énergétique répondant aux enjeux techniques et financiers propres à chaque client.

 Gérer des données énergétiques et financières, apporter un support à l’équipe de construction et veiller à l’atteinte des objectifs du projet tout au long de son cycle de vie.  
 Gérer les attentes des clients, entretenir des relations de confiance et jouer un rôle de référence technique auprès d’eux.

 About the Storage Execution team
 The Storage Execution team sits at the heart of MongoDB’s Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) team. We own the core transactional read/write path on each node, across both today’s storage engine and a next‑generation cloud-native storage architecture. Our work determines how correct and performant MongoDB is for customers running mission-critical production workloads.

 Defining and maintaining the internal collection and index APIs used by Replication, Query and Catalog modules, and commands for local reads and writes, plus the transaction and durability primitives that govern visibility, conflict resolution and crash recovery
 Integrating the next generation of MongoDB’s storage architecture into the server in a way that is predictable for other teams, scales with cloud elasticity, and preserves the performance and safety of the classic configuration
 Improving transaction processing speed and semantics of both single shard and cross-shard transactions
 Owning index builds and schema‑level storage operations (build/rebuild, cleanup, resumability) and ensuring they behave well for large, highly available clusters running write-heavy workloads
 Building validation, diagnostics, and storage‑focused test infrastructure to catch durability issues early and keep the system trustworthy at scale
 Partnering with neighboring teams on flow control, prioritization and load-shedding to stay within resource limits, protecting durability and availability at the cluster level without starving critical operations

 Lead, grow and manage a New York–based team of 8 to 10 engineers; ensure clear expectations, high standards, and healthy, sustainable execution

 Manage customer escalations involving storage behavior and durability; work directly with Support, Atlas, and other server teams to reproduce, root‑cause, and resolve issues

 Partner closely with Replication, Query, Sharding, Catalog & Routing, Storage Engines, and Atlas teams on cross‑team features such as the new storage architecture, availability improvements, and workload management

 Demonstrated customer obsession: direct experience working with demanding customers (or customer support / cloud teams) on complex incidents and turning them into clear, outcome‑oriented recommendations
 Proven ability to develop people: mentoring and promoting engineers, managing underperformance directly, and building high‑engagement teams with low regretted attrition
 Comfortable leading multi‑quarter initiatives with multiple stakeholders and using written documents to align teams on design, scope, and tradeoffs
 Success measures

 Built strong relationships with your team and key partner teams
 Taken over team ceremonies, short‑term planning, and on‑call responsibilities
 Co‑led at least one active project and shipped one concrete process improvement
 In six to twelve months, you have:

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

 Sourcing Strategy & Execution

 ·       Deliver measurable cost savings, cost avoidance and other value improvements while balancing service, quality, operational requirements and risk.
 Rate Management & Commercial Implementation

 ·       Ensure sourcing awards are effectively translated into contracts, purchase orders, catalogues, rate structures and approved buying channels.
 ·       Monitor commercial conditions and identify missing, incorrect or outdated rates, coordinating corrective actions with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
 ·       Resolve Procurement-owned pricing and commercial discrepancies, including price mismatches affecting the three-way-match and payment process.
 ·       Establish effective mechanisms to maintain visibility of pricing, rate validity, contract coverage and commercial performance.
 Vendor Onboarding, Compliance & Enablement

 ·       Identify root causes of recurring purchasing, pricing and payment issues and coordinate corrective actions across relevant stakeholders.
 ·       Support improved Payment on Time (POT) by addressing procurement-related causes of invoice and payment delays.
 Digitalization, AI & Continuous Improvement

 Performance Management & Other Responsibilities

About Liferaft 
 Liferaft builds software that helps organizations find, understand, and act on potential risks from publicly available information. Our clients include corporate security teams around the world, including some of the world’s leading organizations. We’re a remote-first company committed to building a high-performing, values-driven team that operates with clarity, discipline, accountability, and care.
 Liferaft was recently acquired by global security company Securitas, expanding our ability to deliver intelligence-led security at scale. Together, our technology and security solutions help these organizations protect their people, assets, and operations, making a meaningful impact in the world we live in.
 About the Role 
 Liferaft is looking for a highly skilled and visionary Senior Product Manager to play a crucial role in shaping the future of our OSINT solutions. This role will be hybrid in Halifax, NS, or fully remote within the Eastern, or Atlantic time zones in Canada. 
 Reporting to the Chief Innovation Officer, You will be responsible for defining product strategy, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and driving the development of innovative intelligence tools that address our customers' most critical needs. This role requires a deep understanding of OSINT methodologies, strong analytical skills, and the ability to translate complex requirements into user-centric solutions.
What you do as the Senior Product Manager at Liferaft 
 Product Line Strategy & Vision: Define and communicate a compelling product roadmap aligned with company goals and market needs.
 Customer & Market Research: Conduct user research, analyze industry trends, and engage with customers to identify opportunities and pain points.
 Cross-Functional Leadership: Collaborate with engineering, design, marketing, and customer success teams to drive product development and ensure successful execution.
 Continuous Discovery: Ensure that you and the team continue to learn and measure before, during and after a product’s launch phases. 
 Data-Driven Decision Making: Leverage analytics and user feedback to measure product performance and guide iterative improvements.
 Stakeholder Communication: Present product updates, roadmaps, and business cases to executives and key stakeholders.
 Regulatory & Ethical Considerations: Ensure compliance with legal, ethical, and security best practices in OSINT applications.
 Guidance and Mentorship: As a senior member of the Product Team, you will be looked upon for mentorship and guidance related to the product and/or customer and industry problems to solve.
 What You Need to Get the Job Done 
 5+ years of product management experience, preferably in the OSINT, cybersecurity, intelligence, or data analytics space. 
 We will value prior experience in the intelligence space as an intelligence analyst or similar roles.
 Strong technical acumen with an understanding of AI both as an internal enablement tool and embedded in product workflows.
 Proven track record of launching successful B2B SaaS products.
 Experience working with Agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban).
 Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to make data-driven decisions.
 Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
 Passion for intelligence, security, and leveraging technology for actionable insights.
 Why Liferaft? 
  We pride ourselves on our innovative spirit and determination to help solve new challenges developed by the complexities of open source data. Liferaft provides a threat intelligence and investigations platform, Navigator, to corporate security teams around the world, including some of the biggest brands you've probably referenced today! Navigator is designed to identify, track, and validate issues from open source channels (surface, deep web, and darknet) related to executive safety, fraud prevention, and asset & infrastructure protection. Our technology is helping keep these companies, their people, and their operations safe – making a real impact in the world we all live in.
The diversity of our team is integral to our success. We are a team of passionate and supportive individuals and pride ourselves in fostering a collaborative, innovative, and fun culture. 
 We offer our team: 
 Competitive compensation plan 
 Flexible PTO – Our team is encouraged to take a minimum of 15 days/year with no cap beyond
 Hybrid workplace with flexible working hours
 Health & Dental Benefits (Medavie Blue Cross)
 80% employer paid benefits
 Orthodontic coverage for minor dependents 
 Comprehensive mental health coverage, up to $3,000 per year, available for employees and dependents
 Free access to EAP, Greenshield and a variety of physical and mental health services via wellness platform
 $750 Yearly Lifestyle Subsidy
 Monthly cell phone reimbursement
 Monthly parking reimbursement
 Company-sponsored social events and team-building activities
 Strong culture of employee recognition
 Monthly peer-nominated “Cheers” awards with gift card draws
 Quarterly Performance Awards recognizing exceptional impact, collaboration, and innovation
 Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Committee
 Authentic, engaged team, who value work life balance
 Hiring Process: 
 We’re building a company future generations can be proud of. Diversity at Liferaft means fostering a workplace in which individual differences are recognized, appreciated, respected and responded to in ways that fully develop and utilize each person's talents and strengths.
